plate_findings.evidence: bilateral abnormalities of the basal ganglia, thalamus

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial brain MRI from a neonatal HIE patient showing bilateral basal ganglia/thalamic abnormalities marked by red arrows, consistent with stage III HIE. B: Sagittal brain MRI from the same neonatal HIE patient showing brainstem involvement (red arrow), reported as involving the vestibulocochlear nerve nucleus in clinical stage III HIE.

panels.figure_caption: The brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in P9 (Table 4) exhibited bilateral abnormalities of the basal ganglia, thalamus, and brainstem, which are involved in the nucleus of vestibulocochlear nerve with clinical stage III hypoxic–ischemic encephalopathy and profound hearing impairments.
in_text_mentions: s, and three had basal ganglion, thalamus, and midbrain MRI lesions. Diffuse white matter injury was noted in the brain of one patient with HIE and moderate hearing. Among five patients with severe-to-profound hearing loss, three cases were associated with symmetrical thalamus, basal ganglion, midbrain, and brainstem anomalies (Figure 2); one was associated with a subdural hematoma; one had diffuse white matter injury (Table 4). Overall, the degree of hearing loss was reflected in the degree of brain MRI anomalies, except for one profound case of hearing loss without brain parenchymal lesions.

plate_findings.evidence: hypointense punctate confluent white matter lesions in the centrum semiovale

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Axial FSE T2 MRI of a neonatal patient showing punctate confluent white matter lesions in the centrum semiovale, consistent with hypoxic-ischemic white matter injury. B: Axial FSE T2 MRI showing periventricular white matter lesions in a neonatal patient with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. C: Axial MP-RAGE T1 MRI showing hyperintense white matter signal corresponding to the T2 abnormalities, consistent with hypoxic-ischemic injury. D: Axial MP-RAGE T1 MRI showing hyperintense white matter signal corresponding to the T2 abnormalities, consistent with hypoxic-ischemic injury. E: Axial susceptibility-weighted MRI showing rounded small spots of signal intensity in the cerebellar peduncles bilaterally, consistent with infratentorial hemorrhagic injury in hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. F: Axial susceptibility-weighted MRI showing a rounded small spot of signal intensity in the right dentate region, consistent with infratentorial...
panels.attribution_text: Tuoni et al. Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy after acute carbon monoxide intoxication during pregnancy. A case report and brief review of the literature.. Frontiers in pediatrics 2023. doi:10.3389/fped.2023.1264855. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Brain MRI performed at 42 weeks of gestational age shows supratentorial (A–D) and infratentorial (E,F) pattern of brain injury. From left to right, supratentorial axial FSE T2 images (A–D) showing hypointense punctate confluent white matter lesions in the centrum semiovale (A) and in the periventricular white matter (B); axial MP-RAGE T1 images showing hyperintense signal corresponding to the abovementioned T2 signal abnormalities (C,D). Infratentorial axial Susceptibility Weighted images (E,F) shows rounded small spots of signal intensity in the cerebellar peduncles bilaterally (E) and in the right dentate region (F).
in_text_mentions: ial ultrasound showed bilateral persistent non-homogeneous periventricular hyperechogenicity. Brain magnetic resonance imaging was performed and revealed a supratentorial pattern of confluent punctate white matter lesions in the deep and periventricular white matter associated with infratentorial small foci of hemorrhagic injury in the cerebellum (Figure 1). At 3 months of life on neurological objectivity, the spontaneous movement pattern was characterized by sporadic fidgety movements with monotonous repertoire; mild four-limb hypertension was appreciated, with increased deep tendon reflexes.
